source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Amoxicillin suspension 375 mg is ordered. The stock is 250 mg/5 mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
questions.rationale: Desired ÷ stock × volume = 375 ÷ 250 × 5 = 7.5 mL.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Basic pharmacology computations (PDF p. 59)
questions.quote: Desired Dose x Volume = Correct Dose Stock Dose

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Atropine 0.25 mg IM is ordered. The ampule contains 500 mcg/mL. How many mL should be injected?
questions.rationale: 500 mcg = 0.5 mg; 0.25 ÷ 0.5 × 1 mL = 0.5 mL. Convert units first.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Computation problems (PDF p. 58)
questions.quote: Stock: 500 mcg/l ml. ampule

questions.stem: An order reads Penicillin G 1.2 million units IM. When reconstituted, the vial contains 600,000 units per 2 mL. How many mL should be given?
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Basic pharmacology computations (PDF p. 59)
questions.quote: Desired Dose x Volume = Correct Dose Stock Dose

questions.stem: 1,000 mL of D5LR is to run for 8 hours using a macroset (15 gtt/mL). What is the drip rate?
questions.rationale: gtt/min = volume × drop factor ÷ minutes = 1,000 × 15 ÷ 480 ≈ 31.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Computation problems (PDF p. 58)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An insulin drip of 100 units regular insulin in 100 mL NSS runs at 8 mL/hr. How many units does the client receive per hour?
questions.rationale: Concentration = 1 unit/mL; 8 mL/hr × 1 unit/mL = 8 units/hr.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Computation problems (PDF p. 58)
questions.quote: An insulin drip is initiated with 50 units of insulin in 100 mls. of nomal saline solution.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 12-kg child is ordered ampicillin 25 mg/kg per dose IV every 6 hours. How many mg per dose?
questions.rationale: 25 mg × 12 kg = 300 mg per dose (1,200 mg per day).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Computation problems (PDF p. 58)
questions.quote: An Infant who weighs 7.5 kg. is to receive ampicillin (Omnipen) 25mg/kg IV every 6 hrs.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The most accurate way to identify a client before giving medication is to:
options: Check the room and bed number
questions.rationale: Room numbers change, confused clients may answer wrongly, and relatives may be unreliable.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 58)
questions.quote: The most accurate method ofchecking patient identification IS by checking the identification band.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client says, "This blue capsule is not the one I usually take." The nurse should:
options: Withhold it and recheck the order
Ask him to take it later
questions.rationale: Whenever a client doubts a medication, recheck the order before giving it.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 59)
questions.quote: Whenever a client expresses doubt about a medication, the nurse should take it into consideration. She should recheck the medication order.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A nurse realizes she gave a client the wrong medication. What should she do?
questions.rationale: Medication errors require client assessment, notification of the physician, documentation (incident report) and close monitoring.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 59)
questions.quote: Assessment, notification, documentation and close monitoring of the patient are essential.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with difficulty swallowing must take a regular tablet. The best approach is to:
options: Give the whole tablet in a soft food
Dissolve it in a full glass of juice
questions.rationale: Giving the whole tablet in soft food (mashed banana, congee) works; enteric-coated and capsules are not crushed, and unfinished juice means a missed dose.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 59)
questions.quote: administer the whole tablet with soft food such as mashed banana, vanilla pudding , or congee.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: When instilling ear drops in an 8-year-old, the nurse pulls the pinna:
questions.rationale: For children over 3 years and adults, pull the pinna up and back; for younger children, down and back.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 59)
questions.quote: To straighten the ear canal among clients who are above 3 years old, the nurse should pull the pinna up and back.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with renal failure on bumetanide should report which symptom?
questions.rationale: Bumetanide is a potassium-wasting loop diuretic; leg cramps suggest hypokalemia. Give diuretics in the morning.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 60)
questions.quote: Bumex IS potassium uasting diuretic. A potential side-effect in hvpokalenua. as manifested by leg cramps

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Dalteparin (a low molecular weight heparin) is best injected into the:
questions.rationale: Heparin preparations are given subcutaneously, usually in the abdomen; IM injection causes hematoma.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 60)
questions.quote: Daltcpann is a hepann preparation It is administered subcutaneously, such as jn the Iovser abdomen

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client allergic to sulfonamides has several antibiotic orders. Which should the nurse question?
questions.rationale: Cotrimoxazole contains sulfamethoxazole, a sulfonamide.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 60)
questions.quote: It should not be administered in a client With sulfonamide allergy.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which side effect is expected after atropine is given for sinus bradycardia?
questions.rationale: Atropine is anticholinergic: tachycardia, dry mouth, urinary retention, dilated pupils, decreased GI activity.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 60)
questions.quote: Atropine sulfate is an anticholinergic.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An IV infusion has stopped. Which action is incorrect?
options: Checking for kinks in the tubing
questions.rationale: Forceful flushing of a stopped line may push a clot into circulation and cause embolism.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 60)
questions.quote: Flushing the IV needle if the solution stops, may release a blood clot, causing embolism.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An IV site is cool, pale and swollen, and the infusion has stopped. This indicates:
questions.rationale: Infiltration occurs when the cannula leaves the vein; phlebitis causes warmth, redness and pain along the vein.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 61)
questions.quote: These signs and symptoms indicate Infiltration This occurs when the IV needle is out of the vein.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with an IV suddenly becomes dyspneic, hypotensive and confused; air embolism is suspected. After clamping the tubing, the nurse positions him:
options: On the left side, head down
On the right side, head up
questions.rationale: Left lateral Trendelenburg traps air in the right heart and keeps it out of the pulmonary artery.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 62)

Return the blood without telling anyone

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During a transfusion the client develops rash, itching and dyspnea. The nurse's first action is to:
questions.rationale: Stop the blood immediately, keep the line open with saline, then notify and document.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 57)
questions.quote: The client receiving blood transfusion experiences rashes, pruritus, and dyspnea. Which of the following is the best initial nursing action0 a. Stop the transfusion.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When discontinuing a peripheral IV line, the nurse applies pressure to the site with:
questions.rationale: Sterile gauze controls bleeding; alcohol and povidone-iodine irritate the puncture site.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 61)
questions.quote: Use sterile 2x2 gauze to apply pressure at the IV needle site when removing the needle catheter.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A medication label is smudged and unreadable. Who should relabel it?
questions.rationale: Only the pharmacist may relabel medications; nurses never relabel or use unlabeled drugs.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Pharmacology exercises (PDF p. 57)
questions.quote: If the label of the drug is erased or contaminated, who is legally responsible to relabel it? a. the pharmacist
